data.description:
### 2. Incident Overview

**What happened**: Bootstrap-strict run 26542546204 created 12 Jira issues with correct fields and dso-id labels (11/12 labeled), but bindings.json on the tickets branch contains zero bindings ({bindings: {}, reverse: {}}). The BindingStore was loaded by reconcile_once, saved after the pass, but never populated during the pass.

**Root cause**: create_one (applier.py:1452) writes identity labels to Jira via client.add_label and writes mapping.json via _write_mapping_atomic, but does NOT call binding_store.bind(local_id, jira_key). The BindingStore (PR #401) is a separate data structure loaded by reconcile_once (reconcile.py:binding_store = load_binding_store()), but the legacy batch path (_apply_batch -> create_one) has no reference to it.

**Impact**: Without bindings, the outbound differ treats every local ticket as "unbound" on the next pass and tries to create duplicates. The inbound differ skips all Jira issues (only processes bound tickets). Bidirectional sync is broken until bindings are populated.

**Fix approach**: After create_one successfully creates an issue and writes the dso-id label, it should also call binding_store.bind(local_id, jira_key). This requires threading the binding_store through _apply_batch -> create_one, or having reconcile_once populate the binding_store from mapping.json after the apply step.

**code_version:** 99e8ad4ace
data.title: applier: create_one writes dso-id labels but does not populate BindingStore -> bindings.json stays empty
